cells.tense: You are tending the space between people, and you are doing it with the pen in your hand.
cells.ask: Name one specific moment from today when you felt what someone else felt, and say it out loud to them.
cells.core:
Someone tells you something unpolished, and you stay in it with them instead of reaching for the fix. You feel what they feel and still keep your own footing, which is why the unfinished version of the story comes to you and not to everyone. That is the balance this card carries, and it is running now rather than from memory.

The warmth holds because you are not spending yourself to produce it. It works as long as some of what you give goes back into your own side of the exchange, not only out. Keep the receiving end open and this stays easy to carry.
cells.sheetLine: You stay with what people feel without drowning in it.
cells.verb: holding the space where two people actually reach each other
cells.place: the ground of feeling with someone rather than only about them

cells.tense: You are bracing for a version of the room that has not arrived yet, and reacting to it.
cells.ask: Let one person be upset without rearranging anything, and see what happens when you do nothing.
cells.core:
You can feel a rough patch forming before anyone else does, and you are already at work on it — softening the sentence, taking the edge off, getting there ahead of it. It is a generous instinct and it is running well past where it helps. Carry the feeling for two and the other person loses their chance to carry any of it. Connection turns into managing, and managing is not the same as being close.

The steady version stays in the room and lets the upset belong to whoever it belongs to. Their reaction stays theirs, you keep your own footing, and you are still there with them. Difficult feeling gets to be felt by both of you at once — which is the thing you are actually good at when you are not racing it.

cells.tense: You stopped offering what you feel at some point, and you are still standing on that side of it.
cells.ask: Say the plain sentence you would normally leave out to one person today, even if it comes out clumsy.
cells.core:
You can name what someone else is feeling in detail, and your own reactions stay out of the room — agreeing, absorbing, staying easy, and it reads as fine from the outside. The feeling did not stop. The offering did. Being met needs a first move that does not come naturally in a smaller size.

A working exchange runs both directions: you say what you feel as easily as you read what someone else feels, and they get the unpolished version of you the way you get theirs. Neither person absorbed into the other. Get straight with yourself first about what you actually think and feel; that inside steadiness is what makes the step out possible.

cells.tense: You are already the one people settle around, and you talk about it like it is happening to you.
cells.ask: Pick one recent time you deliberately made someone comfortable and say out loud that you did it.
cells.core:
People calm down around you, they say more, they lean in, and you treat it as the atmosphere instead of something you are doing on purpose. You leave a room having steadied it and file it under manners. That reading is too thin.

What a clear version looks like: you feel for someone and you decide what to do with that — steady them, let them be, say the true thing. The warmth is yours and you can point to it, which is what makes it dependable rather than accidental. Calling it yours does not make it less kind; it makes it usable. Watch where the room turns and which way.
cells.sheetLine: You steady the room on purpose, and you call it nothing.
